transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Um, mostly I’m here because I’m just... I'm tired in a way that sleep doesn’t really fix. Like, even just doing normal things, you know, unloading the dishwasher, or trying to read for my certificate class... it all just feels like it's too much right now.
Have you experienced these feelings of exhaustion and difficulty managing daily tasks at any point in your life before this current period?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I've been tired before, like anyone else, but... not quite like this. Usually, if I get a good night's sleep, I bounce back. I haven't really had a time in the past where just doing basic chores felt this impossible. So, no, this level of exhaustion is pretty new to me.
Beyond the exhaustion, have you been feeling unusually worried, anxious, or unable to stop your mind from racing lately?

Um, yeah, actually. I wouldn't say I feel unusually anxious, but my mind definitely races, especially at night. It's like I just can't turn the channel off in my head. I'll be lying there and my thoughts will just jump from, you know, a logo idea, to household chores I need to do, then to a grant proposal, and then suddenly I'm thinking about an argument we’d had. It just keeps bouncing around like that and I can't get it to stop.
Do you find that your symptoms, particularly the exhaustion, get significantly worse after you engage in physical or mental exertion?

Um, I don't really think so. I mean, doing things is hard because I'm already so tired, but I haven't really noticed that doing them makes the exhaustion worse afterward. It's more just a constant feeling, no matter what I do.
Do you find that you have lost interest or pleasure in doing things that you previously enjoyed?

Yeah, I have. I just... I stopped caring about the things that usually make me feel like myself. I haven't been sketching at all, which is weird for me. And I haven't gone to any gallery openings lately. Even just normal stuff, like cooking a nice meal, going to yoga, or playing tennis with a friend... I just have no interest in doing any of it right now.

Looking back over your entire life, can you recall any other periods lasting at least two weeks where you felt this same persistent low mood, lack of energy, or loss of interest in things you usually enjoy?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had days where I felt a little down or tired, but nothing like this that lasted for weeks at a time. This feels different, like it's just sticking around. So, no, I can't really remember another time it was this bad for this long.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or your weight since you started feeling this way?

Yeah, my appetite has definitely been off. Um... sometimes I'll just realize it's late in the afternoon and I've only had coffee and maybe a few bites of food all day. And because of that, my jeans have gotten noticeably looser, even though I haven't been trying to lose weight at all.
On a scale of one to ten, how would you rate your ability to function or get through your day-to-day responsibilities right now?

I guess I'd say maybe a four or a five? It's just... I'm really struggling to keep up with things. I've fallen pretty far behind in my certificate coursework because I just can't seem to stay organized or follow through on anything. And it's bleeding into everything else, too. Bills are piling up, I'm not cooking meals, and the house is a mess. My spouse has had to take over a lot of the stuff at home just to keep us afloat. And like I said before, I've really pulled back from my friends and my art stuff. I just can't manage it right now.
Have you noticed that your movements or your speech have become noticeably slower, or conversely, that you feel physically restless and unable to sit still?

Yeah, I have noticed some changes like that. On my slower days, it just feels like my body is moving through wet cement. Everything takes so much effort. And it's not just moving... even answering a simple question from my spouse can take me a weirdly long time to process and actually get the words out. So, definitely more on the slower side than feeling restless.

Have you ever felt so slowed down that you were unable to speak or move for an extended period, or have you had any experiences where you felt disconnected from reality, such as hearing or seeing things that others could not?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I've never been completely unable to move or speak, just... slower than normal. And I haven't heard or seen things that aren't there or felt disconnected from reality. It's just been the low energy and the slow processing.
Have you been feeling a sense of worthlessness or excessive, inappropriate guilt about things lately?

No, not really. I mean, I feel bad that my spouse is having to do so much around the house right now, but I wouldn't say I feel worthless or... or guilty about things that don't make sense. It's just frustration with myself for not being able to keep up.
Have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living or that you would be better off dead?

No, I haven't had any thoughts like that. I mean, it's definitely frustrating to feel so drained and slow, but I don't feel like life isn't worth living or anything. I don't want to be dead. I just want to feel like myself again.
Aside from your mind racing at night, have you noticed any other changes to your sleep, such as difficulty falling asleep, waking up too early, or perhaps sleeping much more than usual?

No, not really. Aside from having a hard time falling asleep because my mind won't shut off, my sleep has been pretty normal. I'm not waking up super early or sleeping all day. Once I finally do get to sleep, I stay asleep.
How many weeks have you been feeling this way?
This whole pattern has been going on for about four months now. It started right around the time the arguments with my spouse started getting a lot more frequent.
